changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.onFailMessage: A problem has two different identities in problem_lineage. The identity cannot move to the problem. Report this database state as a defect.
preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ( SELECT workspace_id, id FROM ( SELECT workspace_id, problem_id AS id, identity FROM problem_lineage WHERE problem_id IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT workspace_id, prior_problem_id, identity FROM problem_lineage WHERE prior_problem_id IS NOT NULL) named GROUP BY workspace_id, id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT identity) > 1) conflicting

changeSet.comment: The problem now holds its identity, which lineage rows held until now. A lineage row holds the identity of its problem: the newer problem, or the previous one when it is no longer present. Unchanged and Updated rows match both problems by that identity, so both get it. A problem that no row names and that has a key gets "key:" and its key. A problem without a key that no row names keeps no identity, because its identity is a hash of the server's serialization that SQL cannot reproduce exactly.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE problem p SET identity = named.identity FROM ( SELECT workspace_id, problem_id AS id, identity FROM problem_lineage WHERE problem_id IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT workspace_id, prior_problem_id, identity FROM problem_lineage WHERE prior_problem_id IS NOT NULL) named WHERE p.workspace_id = named.workspace_id AND p.id = named.id AND p.identity IS NULL; UPDATE problem SET identity = 'key:' || key WHERE identity IS NULL AND key IS NOT NULL;

rollback.sql: UPDATE problem SET identity = NULL WHERE identity IS NOT NULL;

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: A lineage row reads its identity from its problem, so the copy on the row goes. The rollback copies it back from the problem. A row whose problem has no identity cannot exist: the seal writes the identity, and lineage records it on a previous problem sealed without one.
